acceptance: Typed contracts and evaluators cover exact, ordered/unordered, numeric-tolerance, approximation-bound, valid-set, and semantic-equivalence outcomes.
Cross-engine contracts define null ordering, NaN, timestamp/time-zone, collation, and nested-value equivalence where relevant.
Every outcome uses the manifest's evidence-status vocabulary and only passed evidence is scoreable.
Negative tests prove wrong values, order, tolerance, accuracy, and semantic variants fail closed.
The implementation is reusable by both Power and Throughput evidence paths.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. Numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, thresholds, and the M4 reference remain pilot hypotheses until methodology freeze.
description: Implement the score correctness engine independently of benchmark fixtures. Support exact, ordered and unordered, numeric-tolerance, approximation-bound, valid-set, and semantic-equivalence outcomes, including canonical cross-engine semantics for nulls, NaN, timestamps, collation, and complex values.
